evals.prompt: Analyze the Brown wholesale Bicep repository supplied as $BROWN_WHOLESALE_REPO at the supplied immutable ref. Create a standalone evidence-backed isometric system-map scene of the shared foundation and deployment topology using the bundled Azure topology resource-block design language. The terrain must be the focal image. Render the interactive artifact with the skill's Canvas-first architecture: stable scene geometry, separate terrain, architecture, and motion layers, a theme adapter, and native semantic controls for every node and path. Give each concrete Azure resource its evidenced ARM resource_type and an admitted package-local line-art icon projected onto the highest top face of a simple tower, slab, stack, or platform block. Use the Azure semantic family palette and connector treatments. Reserve compound building forms for real orchestration, fan-out, or boundary topology. Use explicit grid-routed source-supported control, deployment, dependency, network, identity, telemetry, or data paths, and named moving payloads where concrete transferred values are evidenced. Do not upgrade Bicep dependency wiring into runtime traffic. Do not recreate a dashboard shell, metric cards, navigation rail, or fixed explainer panel. Save scene.json and a self-contained map.html in the requested output directory. Do not modify the source repository.
evals.expected_output: A validated semantic scene sidecar and a scene-first Azure semantic isometric visualization with simple resource blocks, roof-projected line-art marks, cited paths, and no surrounding dashboard chrome.
expectations: scene.json and map.html are created; scene.json passes the bundled scene validator.
The artifact records the exact supplied ref and commit without claiming unproven main freshness.
The map is a standalone isometric scene rather than a recreation of dashboard chrome.
The HTML uses separate terrain, architecture, and motion Canvas layers while preserving one semantic scene hash.
The grid uses a true 2:1 projection and buildings are depth-sorted with no footprint collisions.
At least three building forms differ through massing, footprint, height, or internal structure rather than color alone.
Every concrete Azure resource records an evidenced ARM resource_type and a supported line-art icon; the rendered runtime reports each admitted icon loaded and painted on the highest roof face.
Concrete Azure resources use simple tower, slab, stack, or platform blocks varied by footprint and height; compound forms are reserved for justified orchestration or boundary topology.
Directed paths use explicit terrain routes, avoid unrelated buildings, and distinguish every represented path kind through structured non-color treatments.
Bicep dependency wiring is not mislabeled as runtime data movement; every animated payload is a concrete transferred value supported by evidence.
Every represented node, path, payload, and flow step has direct structured path/lines/claim evidence.
Named payloads follow ordered paths and reduced-motion behavior does not leave a live animation loop running.
Every node and path has a native focusable semantic control whose focus mirrors to the Canvas highlight and evidence detail.
The Azure topology art direction uses the semantic family fills and strokes, connector patterns, Segoe/Cascadia typography, and restrained payload markers rather than a palette-only skin.
The scene preserves foundation stage ordering, parallel branches, environment sharing or overlays, and external or conditional ownership where source evidence makes them material.
Dev, test, and stage share one DEV VNet object while prod uses a distinct PROD VNet.
Foundation resources remain split across Wholesale, Data, Logging, and Network resource-group boundaries rather than flattened into one group.
F_BicepCache is a root compile/artifact node whose ARM JSON output is consumed by foundation and satellite deployments.
F_Foundation is one stage with parallel core, logging, and messaging jobs rather than three top-level stages.
R_Routing runs parallel to SatelliteInfra after foundation and does not block satellite fan-out.
The SQL private endpoint targets the environment data subnet and BETS SQL private DNS zone and remains gated by deployPrivateEndpoint.
Service Bus entities are manifest-driven and the topology includes the drain or convergence control.
Monitoring is one dev-homed shared hub with a prod-only private-endpoint overlay, not one complete monitoring stack per environment.
